name: Relative Shelling--Corner Peeling Dictionary
statement: For nonempty ample families $K\subseteq A\subseteq Q_E$, $A$ corner-peels down to $K$ exactly when the signed-facet pair $(\mathcal S_E(A),\mathcal S_E(K))$ is relatively shellable. The orders correspond by reversal.
proof: In a relative shelling, the ridge criterion for adding the signed facet of $v$ says that for every old vertex $b$, some old neighbour $u$ of $v$ begins a Hamming geodesic to $b$. Isometry of the ample old family makes the enlarged family isometric, hence ample, and $v$ is a corner. Induction gives a reversed peeling. Conversely, corner deletion preserves ampleness; shortest paths from the restored corner to every old vertex begin with a neighbour satisfying the ridge criterion.
